title: Additivity in the coefficients
statement:
Fix a field $K$ and natural numbers $n, D$, and write $\mathcal{S}_{n,D}$ for the type of subsets $s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ with $\abs{s} \le D$. For a coefficient function $c \colon \mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K$, let $P(c)$ denote the multivariate polynomial $\sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}_{n,D}} c(s)\, \prod_{i \in s} X_i$ over $K$ in the variables $X_0, \dots, X_{n-1}$. Then for any finite index set $S$ and any family of coefficient functions $(c_i)_{i \in S}$ with each $c_i \colon \mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K$, the polynomial built from the pointwise sum of coefficients equals the sum of the individual polynomials:
\[
P\!\left(\sum_{i \in S} c_i\right) = \sum_{i \in S} P(c_i).
\]
hypotheses_covered: S is a finite index set over an arbitrary type ι
a family of coefficient functions c_i : LowDegreeSupport n D → K indexed by S
